findings.title: Federated recovery credential is not removed when all codes are used
findings.body: After a successful recovery-code login, RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential can return a credential supplied by a user-storage provider. If all codes are used, the code calls authenticatedUser.credentialManager().removeStoredCredentialById(...), which only removes credentials stored in Keycloak's local storage. A federated/user-storage credential will therefore not be removed or disabled. This can leave an exhausted recovery-code credential configured in the external storage and can break assumptions in later code that the credential no longer exists. A storage-aware disable/remove path should be used instead of removeStoredCredentialById.

findings.title: Unsafe Optional/get calls can cause NoSuchElementException during login
findings.body: RecoveryAuthnCodeInputLoginBean calls credentialModelOpt.get() without checking whether RecoveryAuthnCodesUtils.getCredential(user) returned a credential, and then calls getNextRecoveryAuthnCode().get() without checking that an unused code exists. If the credential is absent, or if a user-storage provider reports a recovery credential with no remaining unused codes, rendering the recovery-code login page throws NoSuchElementException and results in a 500 error instead of a graceful failure or redirect to credential setup.

findings.title: Possible NullPointerException when recovery-code form fields are missing
findings.body: processAction reads generatedRecoveryAuthnCodes and generatedAt from the form and immediately calls generatedAtTimeString.equals(...) and generatedCodesString.equals(...). If a client submits the required-action request without those hidden fields, the method throws NullPointerException instead of treating the submission as invalid and re-challenging. Null checks or null-safe comparisons are needed.

findings.title: User-storage recovery codes are not consumed and single-use behavior is not tested
findings.body: The test storage validates a recovery code by comparing the raw input against stored raw codes and never records that the code was consumed. getCredentials also rebuilds the credential from the raw list, so the credential always appears unused. As a result, a recovery code accepted once remains valid indefinitely for this user-storage implementation. Recovery codes are intended to be single-use, but the added test only performs one successful login and therefore does not verify consumption. The test/provider should enforce and verify one-time use, or the core changes need a mechanism to mark federated recovery codes as used.

findings.title: getCredentials does not preserve credential ID or usage state
findings.body: BackwardsCompatibilityUserStorage.getCredentials deserializes the stored recovery-code JSON and calls RecoveryAuthnCodesCredentialModel.createFromValues(...) without copying the stored CredentialModel's ID or any used-state. The returned credential therefore has a transient or missing ID and always appears unused. Code that relies on the credential ID to remove/disable the credential, or on used flags to compute the next recovery-code number, will not work correctly with this storage.
